reading.title: Premolars, supporting bone structure and orthodontic brackets
reading.text: A premolar is a dual-cusped permanent tooth located between the canine and molar teeth used to tear and crush food. Gingiva surrounds necks, and sockets hold roots. The orthodontist evaluates the alignment of the first premolar. Alveolar bone is the specialized thickened ridge of the jawbone containing tooth sockets that support and anchor tooth roots. Pulp houses nerves, and maxilla forms the upper jaw. Periodontal disease can cause gradual loss of alveolar bone height. The dental arch is the curved parabolic arrangement formed by the complete row of teeth in either the upper or lower jaw. Mandible forms the lower jaw, and brackets attach to enamel. The orthodontist assesses crowding across the upper dental arch. Orthodontic braces use metal or ceramic attachments and flexible archwires to apply gentle pressure and move misaligned teeth. A retainer holds positions, and an aligner is removable. The teenager wears ceramic braces to straighten overlapping incisors. An orthodontic bracket is a small slotted metal or ceramic attachment bonded directly to each tooth surface to hold the archwire. A wire applies force, and rubber bands hook arches. The orthodontist bonds a tiny bracket to the central incisor.
